title: CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
body: Ms. Kamali reported on the following: She extended a sincere congratulations to the newly elected members of the Commission. Interval International is donating 40 to 50 nonperishable Thanksgiving food boxes for residents in need. The City's Thanksgiving Turkey Drive is scheduled for Wednesday, November 16th for City residents only. The Santa's Parade of Elves is Sunday, December 4th at 2:00 pm. South Miami Grey Ghosts Peewee and 11 & under teams won their semifinal games and will move on to the championship game on Saturday, November 19th. The South Miami Grey Ghost Varsity Cheerleaders won second place at the Orange Bowl Cheer Competition. An FDOT construction project is scheduled to start December 7th from 80th Street to 57th Avenue which consists of signalization improvement and pedestrian crossing improvement throughout the corridor. City Hall will be closed on Thursday, November 24th and Friday, November 25th for the Thanksgiving Holiday. The Parking Division is preparing 20 passes for the library to provide to individuals that are attending library sponsored programs. She clarified that item #8 is for discussion only.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Pepe reported on the following: He stated that they are working on the condominium conversion of the parking garage, the survey should be completed by November 27th. Also, he is working with an outside attorney that specializes in condominium conversion to complete the Articles of Incorporation. Other documents that need to be prepared are Declaration of Condominium, by-laws of the association on the rules and regulations. Mr. Pepe also explained the McCormick and Stunna's Fit cases to the Commission. At Commissioner Liebman's request, Mr. Pepe explained the approved Charter amendments from the November 8th election. Mayor Fernández requested that Mr. Pepe provide a status report on the open litigation cases to the Commission. As it relates to item #12, the original ordinance, Ordinance No. 21-21-2411, the vote was 4-1, with former Mayor Philips voting nay.

title: PUBLIC REMARKS
body: The following spoke during public remarks: Kevin Greiner, Philip Stoddard, Gray Read, Katrina Erwin, Nicole Gazo, Ian Querton, Jorge Milian, Sally Philips, Anna Price, Joe Barros, Antoinette Fischer, Gabriel Varona, Marissa Berio LeBeau, John Edward Smith, and Walter Harris.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Liebman commented on the following: congratulated the all candidates on running great campaigns; mentioned the cost of the election compared to past elections; commended the residents for approving the four charter amendments and asked that the Commission at a later date revisit the Mayor's term charter amendment; stated that the items on the agenda are for discussion; mentioned that he is giving his appointment to the Planning Board to Vice Mayor Bonich; and thanked Ms. Kamali for service and friendship as this is her last in-person Commission meeting. Commissioner Calle commented on the following: stated that it is an honor to serve on the Commission and as a promise he made while campaigning that he will try to keep the culture of South Miami as the new phase progresses; also mentioned that he is an electrical engineer and he believes in solar power and the only question that he had regarding this is solar insurance that he will look into. Commissioner Corey commented on the following: thanked everyone for coming to the meeting; and welcomed the new Commission members. Vice Mayor Bonich thanked everyone for electing her and she looks forward to serving the City. Mayor Fernández thanked everyone for attending the Commission meeting and commenting; stated that he doesn't agree with all the items on the agenda but does agree that a lot of improvements will come of the conversations; and stated that he is honored and is looking forward to working with the Commission building on good foundation laid by his predecessors.

title: CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
body: Deputy Manger Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: She stated that item #4 will be pulled from the agenda because Interval International could not be present tonight. Fourteen state attorneys from Kathern Rundle's office trained with Police Department Senior Trainer Al Alvarez and Sgt. Edgardo Bartra utilizing the department's specialized stimulator for life and death split-second decision-making scenarios. The Police Department extended an invitation to the City Commission to participate in the training as well. A live active shooting training scenario was conducted at Larkin Hospital, in order to train the hospital staff on how to react should there be a large-scale event. The training enhanced the abilities of the South Miami Police personnel in responding to such an event. This training was conducted by Al Alvarez and Det. Jose Alvarez. The Police Department will have accessors present between December 12, 2022 and December 15, 2022, as the department moves towards reaccreditation by the Commission of Florida Law Enforcement. Office Rodney Napier secured $21,900.00 in funding from South Miami Hospital to procure the department's two emergency shelter beds and related services, which this year achieved 100% utilization rate and now extends the program from December 1, 2022 to November 2023. The City's Parade of Elves was held on Sunday, December 4, 2022. A special thanks to the Parks & Recreation and Public Works Departments for a successful event. The City's annual Toy Give-away is scheduled for Wednesday, December 14, 2022 at 3:00 pm at the Bethel-Gibson Community Center. Registration is now open for Winter Break Camp, Co-ed Youth Basketball, Baseball and Volleyball Clinics. An FDOT construction project started on Monday, December 5, 2022 north of SW 80th Street to South Riviera Drive, traveling lanes and sidewalks are scheduled to be closed during non-peak hours. Three public meetings will be held by the Miami-Dade County Department of Transportation and Public Works regarding Phase 3 of The Underline. Jose Fuentes and Max Losner of Beckler Polikaff, the City’s lobbyist, presented an outline of some of last year legislature priorities. The three main ones are the pedestrian bridge project. The City requested $2 million and was awarded $1 million for construction and $400,000 for engineering and inspection, scheduled for fiscal year 2025; $500,000 was requested for the culvert replacement at SW 64th Court within the Twin Lakes canal, nothing has been awarded at this time; $5 million was requested for the police station, $3 million was awarded at the State level but was vetoed by the Governor before adoption of the State's budget. Jose Fuentes, Manny Reyes, and Max Losner the City's lobbyists gave an update of the legislative time lines, funding sources and opportunities for the City. title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Liebman extended condolences to Commissioner Walter Harris on the loss of his wife; spoke about Commander Michael McVeigh's accomplishments; spoke about the successful Santa's Parade of the Elves; asked that the Commission listen to items objectively; suggested the City consider updating the bike bollards and garbage cans along the commercial core to compliment the new benches; and recommended a friendly kickball game between the Commission and staff. Vice Mayor Bonich thanked staff for the success of the parade and enjoyed it as her first event as Vice Mayor. Commissioner Corey thanked everyone for their diverse comments; spoke about the success of the parade and how the businesses/restaurants reap the benefits of events like this; and spoke about the success of the library and their partnership with the City. Commissioner Calle mentioned the successful holiday event with the seniors at the Senior Center and Metro South facilities; commented on the success of the parade; and spoke about continuing the process to promote the businesses so they can succeed. Mayor Fernández extended condolences to former Commissioner Harris and Commander McViegh families; thanked staff for assisting him with his agenda items; commended Officer Napier for securing the grant funding for the homeless; mentioned the three meetings regarding The Underline and encouraged the community to engage and get involved; stated he is committed to all parks to substantially improve; and clarified that contract for the city manager is for a short period of time because of advertising deadlines and if someone is chosen tonight a multiyear contract will come back to the Commission for approval. At this time, Mr. Anthony Ferguson addressed the Commission to thanked everyone for their assistance in helping him in his time of need.

title: A Resolution by the Mayor and City Commissioners of the City of South Miami appointing a City Manager and authorizing the Mayor to negotiate and execute an employment contract that is substantially the same as the attached Exhibit A. 3/5 (Mayor Fernández)

votes.motion: approve as amended Resolution No. 168-22-15921 by the Mayor and City Commissioners of the City of South Miami appointing a City Manager and authorizing the Mayor to negotiate and execute an employment contract that is substantially the same as the attached Exhibit A

body: Mayor Fernández mentioned that fifteen candidates applied by the deadline. He suggested eliminating the following four candidates because they don't have the required municipal management experience, Fred Vella, Emmanuel Adediran, Horace Feliu and Allene Haynie and to focus on the remaining eleven candidates. The eleven candidates are Andrea Agha, Mark Kutney, Genaro "Chip" Iglesias, Stanley Hawthorne, Brian Geoghegan, David Couch, Ivian Cao, Juan 'JC' Jimenez, Mario Diaz, Christopher Russo and Kenneth Haskin. Of the eleven candidates Mayor Fernández recommended Genaro 'Chip' Iglesias for the city manager position. Commissioner Calle stated that his top three candidates are Genaro 'Chip' Iglesias, Juan 'JC' Jimenez and Christopher Russo. Commissioner Corey's short list includes Genaro ‘Chip’ Iglesias, Mario Diaz, Christopher Russo, Juan ‘JC’ Jimenez and Andrea Agha. Vice Mayor Bonich's top two candidates are Genaro 'Chip' Iglesias and Juan 'JC' Jimenez. After the discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Liebman and seconded by Commissioner Calle to narrow the list down to two candidates, Genaro 'Chip' Iglesias and Juan 'JC' Jimenez. The motion passed unanimously. After more discussion on the two candidates, it was moved by Mayor Fernández and seconded by Commissioner Liebman to appoint Genaro 'Chip' Iglesias as city manager and execute the contract. The motion passed unanimously. Moved by Mayor Fernández, seconded by Commissioner Corey, the motion to approve as amended Resolution No. 168-22-15921 by the Mayor and City Commissioners of the City of South Miami appointing a City Manager and authorizing the Mayor to negotiate and execute an employment contract that is substantially the same as the attached Exhibit A passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:             Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Calle Commissioner Corey Commissioner Liebman Mayor Javier Fernández Nay:             None

title: CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
body: Mrs. Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: The Police Department passed the reaccreditation by the Commission of Law Enforcement; they were found to be 100% in compliance. The FDOT project north of SW 80th Street to South Rivera Drive continues but, construction activity will be suspended as Friday, December 23rd and will resume on Tuesday, January 3rd. The City was awarded the distinguished Budget Presentation Award for the October 1, 2022 budget by the Government Finance Officers Association. In observance of the Christmas and New Year Holidays, City Hall will be closed on Friday, December 23rd at 12 Noon, Monday, December 26th all day, Friday, December 30th at Noon and Monday, January 2nd all day. At the request of Commissioner Corey, the City will host a Martin Luther King, Jr breakfast on Monday, January 16, 2023 from 10:00 am until 12 Noon at Jean Willis Park.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Pepe reported that the parking garage was recently converted to condominium form of ownership. The declaration, by-laws and articles of incorporation have all been filed. He mentioned that he has attended a webinar regarding the Constitution amendment that prohibits Commission members from lobbying which takes effect in the new year.

title: PUBLIC REMARKS
body: The following spoke during public comments: Walter Harris, Sally Philips, John Edward Smith and Rickelle Collier.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Calle thanked the Police Department on the great work and response relating to the bomb threat at Somerset Charter School. He wants to work with the Commission to get more foot traffic and more sales in the Downtown area. Commissioner Liebman thanked Interval International for their generous donations for the City's toy drive. At this point, item #1 was read and approved. Marcos Agostini addressed the Commission and thanked the Commission for recognizing Interval International. The Commission presented the Interval International Proclamation to Mr. Agostini. Commissioner Corey mentioned that he attended the promotion ceremony for Sgt. Bosch and thanked the City for the MLK, Jr. event. Vice Mayor Bonich congratulated the Police Department and Finance Department for their great achievements. Mayor Fernández also commended the Police Department on how they responded to the school bomb threat and thanked Parks & Recreation Director Quentin Pough for their support of the Police Department at that time; congratulated the Police Department on the reaccreditation and the Finance Department on their award; acknowledge Parks & Recreation for the recent successful senior events; and congratulated his high school, Christopher Columbus on winning the football championship.

title: Chief Rene Landa - Monthly Update PD Recruiting/Hiring Report
body: Chief Landa reported that the FY23 budget allows for 50 sworn officers and 7 communication officers. Currently the department has 42 sworn officers and 1 part-time sworn officer. There are five communication officers, which includes two newly hires that are in the training process. Two law enforcement applicants are currently being processed and should be completed by the end of January. One law enforcement officer has resigned, and one communication officer resigned. There have been no new hire of law enforcement and three more communications officers have applied and are being processed for the last two positions. Mayor Fernández suggested as the next step, having a Committee of the Whole (COW) regarding this subject and invite representatives from the bargaining units, the Police Benevolent Association (PBA) and the Fraternal Order of Police (FOP) to discuss financial mechanisms to entice individuals to apply with the City.

title: Honorable Senator Alexis Calatayud
body: Senator Calatayud reported on the committees that she sits on. other: continued maintenance of the additional drainage facilities (e
body: Please note that items #6 and #7 were taken together. It was noted that Sally Philips submitted an email relating to the imperious coverage on item #6. City Attorney Recio read the quasi-judicial proceedings for this item and swore in everyone that will speak on these two items. Planning Director Hank Flores presented the staff report to the Commission. Mr. James M. Schiff on behalf of the applicant addressed the Commission. He pointed out that there is a project at 7031 SW 76 Street, which is adjacent to his client's property. A resolution was approved in 2016 for the approval of that project that is similar to this project, and he asked that this variance is approved. The following spoke during the public hearing on this item: Dick Ward. After the discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Liebman and seconded by Commissioner Corey to deny the request for the variance. The motion failed by a 2-3 vote (Yea- Commissioner Liebman, Commissioner Corey; Nay-Vice Mayor Bonich, Commissioner Calle, & Mayor Fernández). It was moved by Mayor Fernández and seconded by Commissioner Calle to approve with two conditions, 1) to require the use of pervious pavers consisting of a material acceptable to the Planning Director in the pool area and 2) agree to proffer a covenant to ensure that there is continued maintenance of the additional drainage facilities (e.g. catch basins, grading, drains, etc.) and no negative impacts on the adjacent properties. The motion passed unanimously. Moved by Mayor Fernández, seconded by Commissioner Calle, the motion to approve as amended RESOLUTION NO. 001-23-15935 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA RELATING TO A VARIANCE APPLICATION TO INCREASE THE MAXIMUM IMPERVIOUS COVERAGE REQUIREMENT FOR A NEW TWO-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DWELLING LOCATED AT 6021 SW 76 STREET passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:              Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:              None

title: CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
body: Ms. Kamali thanked the Commission and the City for the last nine years. Ms. Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: The City hosted a successful breakfast honoring Dr. Martin L. King, Jr. at Jean Willis Park on Monday, January 16th. Paseo Park is on track for completion for Monday, January 23rd and a ribbon cutting ceremony is tentative scheduled for Friday, January 27th, once finalized it will be noticed. The City will officially welcome new City Manager Chip Iglesias on Friday, January 20th with a swearing-in ceremony.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Pursuant to Florida Statue 286.011 (8), Ms. Arango requested an Executive Session with the Commission on a pending litigation matter styled Stunna's Fit, LLC vs. the City of South Miami, Case No. 2022-00035 AP 01, coordinated through the City Clerk and City Manager. Mayor Fernández asked the attorneys to provide an update on the parking garage condominium in early February.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Liebman suggested having an art show at Dante Fascell Park the following weekend after the Beaux Arts Festival; spoke of bringing an item to the next Commission meeting implementing the Place Making Study in the downtown area; thanked outgoing city manager Ms. Kamali for her service and mentioned that it has been a pleasure working with Deputy City Manager Fraga-Lopez. Commissioner Calle thanked staff for a successful MLK event. He also thanked Ms. Kamali for her assistance with his transition to Commissioner and looking forward to working with the new city manager. Commissioner Corey supported Commissioner Liebman's idea of an art festival at Dante Fascell Park; thanked everyone for the successful MLK event; also thanked Ms. Kamali; mentioned that he spoke with Ms. Fraga-Lopez about identifying public spaces in the downtown area to put some donated art; and spoke about the opening of Paseo Park. Vice Mayor Bonich thanked American Legion for a wonderful celebration of life for Mr. McVeigh; spoke of the best time she had at the MLK event; and spoke about bringing forward at the next Commission meeting the Age-Friendly Cities and Communities Program that she learned about from the Mayor's office. Mayor Fernández shared that he and Mr. Iglesias will be meeting with University of Miami President Julio Frenk, and asked that the city attorneys facilitate on how to solicit collaboration ideas from the rest of the Commission to comply with the sunshine law; suggested scheduling a meeting to discuss legislative priorities to submit in time for the legislative session; spoke about the success of the MLK event; asked for an annexation update at the next meeting; suggested designating the park near the Family Dollar after Dr. Anna Price in recognizing her role as the first African-American Mayor and to have a black history event at the park to commemorate the designation; and also thanked Ms. Kamali for her services to the City.

title: CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (CIP) PRESENTATION
body: Aurelio Carmenates, Public Works & Engineering Director, gave an overview of the current projects from the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) 5-YR Plan. Mayor Fernández suggested the following regarding CIP: revisit the Sunset Drive Pedestrian Lighting Design idea; regarding the culvert, asked that enforcement is stepped up on the truck crossing; would like to stop the process of the design of the pedestrian bridge, rather use the money towards enhancing the crossing; regarding the sanitary sewer, need to establish a financing plan; on the road resurfacing and sidewalk repair, do an inventory of the existing conditions of the streets and sidewalks proactively and to get a cost to do it on a consistence basis on a scale that would make an impact; on the drainage improvements, look into adding the intersection of 57th and 74th Street that floods heavily; and regarding traffic calming circles and devices for the neighborhoods, suggested having a subsequent presentation on why the City is not meeting the criteria for Miami-Dade County standards to install the improvements. Commissioner Calle questioned the criteria for the sidewalk improvements and what has been done historically to move forward; echoed the Mayor's comments with regard to the Sunset Drive Pedestrian Lighting Design and the pedestrian bridge. Vice Mayor Bonich suggested moving forward with the discussion of the City as a whole with regards to landscaping enhancing projects. Commissioner Corey wanted to know the criteria for the drainage projects. Also mentioned that a lot of energy needs to go towards the septic to sewer project. After the discussion, the Commission gave direction to the city manager to stop expending funds for the pedestrian bridge and the Sunset Drive pedestrian lighting design.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Calle spoke about the success of the recent Bougainvillea's Beer Festival. Commissioner Corey thanked everyone for attending the opening of Paseo Park; spoke of the biannual census of homelessness with the Homeless Trust, there was a 35% in reduction of homelessness in the City; and thanked the Urban Related Group on training of the applicants to get better paying jobs. Commissioner Liebman spoke about bringing items forward at a future Commission meeting regarding the banner policy, placemaking/streetscape, and garbage/solid waste. Vice Mayor Bonich thanked PUB 52 for hosting School of Rock latest performances; thanked the city manager and Public Works Department for wonderful cleanup job; and thanked the Police Department for keeping the City safe after a recent incident that made the news. Mayor Fernández thanked Vice Mayor Bonich for her efforts in getting the funding for boys and girls to go to State with the American Legion; thanked Laura Carrasco Perez, Principal of Ludlam Elementary for greeting him recently and that their PTA is also looking for donations; also recognized Public Works for the cleanup job behind the library; mentioned meetings with UM President Frenk on how this community can receive spaces/places that they can't accommodate on campus, and leveraging some competencies from their various departments; spoke of the meeting with Miami-Dade County Commissioner Regalado with regards to the City's annexation application, first phase of sanitary sewer and formalizing a joint disposition with the library through an interlocal agreement; and lastly mentioned that Senator Alexis Calatayud has solicited the Commission's feedback on SB 102 regarding affordable housing. He later mentioned that the Winn Dixie Project that was approved, Fresh Market is now anchoring the project moving forward. As part of the process, there will be some modifications to the TODD market district regulations that will go before the Planning Board and then the City Commission.

body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Liebman thanked the following: the city attorneys for the wonderful job that they are doing; the real estate group for the development of the grocery store mixed-use project; and the City Commission for representing the City well on their recent trip to Tallahassee. Commissioner Corey congratulated the Police Department on their reaccreditation and the Parks & Recreation Department on their recent events; spoke about the successful trip to Tallahassee; and mentioned that the library hosts monthly meetings regarding homelessness. Commissioner Calle spoke of the Tallahassee trip and stated that the Miami-Dade District 7's Mom & Pop grant submittal deadline has been extended to March 24, 2023. Vice Mayor Bonich thanked Public Works Department for fixing the sidewalk in front of the bank; spoke of the successful recent arts festival; congratulated the Police Department on their reaccreditation; and mentioned that the rooftop movie event was very nice event. Mayor Fernández mentioned the successful trips to Tallahassee and St. Augustine; thanked the Parks & Recreation and Public Works Departments for their great work; spoke in favor of Senate Bill 102 which will provide much need revenue for affordable and workforce housing throughout the State; and mentioned that Senate Bill 170 is a bill that the City should watch and advocate for.

title: Vice Mayor Bonich - Ordinance protecting iguanas, peacocks and other invasive species due to citizen complaints.
body: Vice Mayor Bonich explained that residents have been complaining about the iguanas and peacocks. She suggested creating a notice to educate the residents on how to deal with them. City Attorney Arango reported that Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission has guidelines on how to remove iguanas and noted that they are not protected species. With regards to the peacocks, the Commission directed the city attorneys to bring back to the Commission a proposed mitigation policy.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: As regards to Police recruiting and hiring for the vacant positions, there are three applicants that are scheduled to graduate from the Police Academy on April 18th. If those candidates are hired that will leave three vacant positions. The Communications division is fully staffed. The Marshall Williamson Scholarship application will be available starting Monday, March 27, 2023. The Hometown/TODD/Commercial Area Study Workshop is scheduled for Tuesday, March 28, 2023 at 7:00 pm. As a response to Commissioner Liebman regarding the team building, goals and vision session, Mr. Iglesias said that he would also add strategic planning to this session and would provide the Commission on the dates for the session. Commissioner Liebman also asked for an update on the crosswalks. Mr. Iglesias mentioned that Mr. Carmenates has quotes for the crosswalk at 73rd Street, but there need to be a concept of how to striping should be done. Mr. Iglesias gave an update on the Miami-Dade County’s Red Road and Sunset Drive intersection project which should be completed in the summer. Mayor Fernández asked for information regarding the timeline for police officers that will retire soon. Also requested numbers regarding raising base salaries to see what it cost before going into budget season.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: Pickleball will start on April 5 - May 26, 2023 at Gibson Bethel Community Center on Wednesdays and Fridays from 10:00 am - noon. The Easter Egg Hunt is scheduled for Friday, April 7, 2023 from 5:30 pm - 7:00 pm. Family Sensory Room ribbon cutting is scheduled for Friday, April 14, 2023 at 4:00 pm. Chief Rena Landa received a Leadership Award recognition from the Miami-Dade Association of Police Chiefs. Lieutenant Robert Bukens received the Chief's award, he was lead in the reaccreditation process. Chief Landa stated that they have completed the background on three officers that are in the academy and will graduate on April 25, 2023, and April 26, 2023 is their start date with the City. This will bring the number of police officers to 47 with three vacancies.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio reported that they are working on a response regarding the Stunna's Fit’s case after representatives of Stunna's Fit submitted a counter offer to the original settlement offer after the last executive session. Regarding the parking garage, he stated that they are proceeding with the direction of the Commission to get the surveyors to modify the drawings and the legal description and then an amendment of the declaration.

title: PUBLIC REMARKS
body: The following individuals spoke during public remarks: Gail Alexander, Dr. Anna Price, Valtena Gibson-Brown, Dr. Philip Stoddard and John Edward Smith.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commissioner remarks: Commissioner Calle mentioned that he was a judge at a kids entrepreneur contest with 50 kids pitching their businesses and selling their products and services, with Miami-Dade Commissioner Raquel Regalado and her team. He would like to bring this idea to South Miami. At the Marshall Williamson Business Facility (Mobley building), he plans to setup an entrepreneur skills training in teaching business, marketing, develop and finance to the community, along with credit repair, consulting and other teaching abilities. He also stated that he is working with Commissioner Regalado and her team on an kids project where entrepreneur is a focus with Bank of America that teaches kids a lot of different skill sets. Commissioner Corey thanked Dr. Anna Price for all of the great things she has done for the community; mentioned the opening of the Family Sensory Room; and spoke about potentially using some off the streetscape design from Avalon Bay on SW 73rd Street and SW 58th Avenue and submitting those plans to FDOT. Vice Mayor Bonich congratulated Chief Landa; thanked Yvette Valdez, Senior Coordinator, for taking the seniors to the Frost Museum and mentioned that she is working on offering senior residents free Parks & Recreation classes. Mayor Fernández mentioned that he is honored to name green space after Dr. Anna Price and would like to bring the item at the next meeting with a full Commission; thanked Chief Landa for the traffic enforcement on US1 and SW 62nd Avenue, the recruitment efforts and on his leadership award; spoke about the donor funds item to assist the seniors and children of the community; thanked Commissioner Calle for the entrepreneurship item; and thanked the City's leadership.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: The Police Department presented Unit Citation Awards to the Criminal Investigations Division, Lt. Jesus Aguiar, Sgt. Fernando Bosch, Detective Matt Taylor, Detective Jose Alvarez, and Detective Victor Jackson. The Officer of the Year Award was awarded to Detective Jose Alvarez. A swearing in ceremony is scheduled for Friday, April 28th at 2:00 pm for three new police officers. The Arbor Day event is scheduled for Friday, April 28th at 10:00 am at Veterans Park.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio reported that the parking garage survey is proceeding. With regards to the Stunna's Fit case, there is still back and forth with the attorneys, and he will be meeting with their counsel on April 19, 2023.

title: PUBLIC REMARKS
body: The following individuals spoke during public remarks: Dick Ward and Jalen Applewhite.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of the Commission reports: Commissioner Liebman thanked Mr. Applewhite for attending the meeting; thanked staff for the presentation on Solid Waste; and spoke about annexation. Commissioner Calle spoke about the great feedback received as it relates to his initiative regarding financial literacy; acknowledged and thanked Commissioner Corey and Miami-Dade Commissioner Raquel Regalado on the opening of The Sensory Lab; and congratulated the Police Officers on receiving awards. Vice Mayor Bonich congratulated and thanked the Police Department for all their accomplishments. Mayor Fernandez mentioned his recent trip to Tallahassee to discuss the City's legislative items; stated that he has a meeting scheduled with Commissioner Regalado to discuss city hall and the library on how to improve the physical plan of these assets; also mentioned the meeting with the Chair of School Board to discuss the same of how to leverage the assets; congratulated Commissioner Corey on the opening of the Sensory Room; congratulated Chief Landa on the efforts of recruitment and the recent traffic operations on SW 62nd & US1; and thanked staff for responding quickly to the Commission demands. Commissioner Corey thanked Public Works for all their work related to the recent bad weather; thanked Sunset Opportunities for donating a shelter bed at Camillus House for a year; and presented a video of the grand opening of the Sensory Room.

title: Senator Alexis Calatayud (via Zoom)
body: Senator Calatayud reported on the following: Senate Bill 102 passed, the Live Local Act, an Affordable Housing Policy. Senate Bill 994 passed which will create more severe critical penalties for ethnic or religious intimidation, threat to harm or harassment. Senate Bill 942 passed which works to support teachers. Sea level rise studies were also passed during this legislative session; every new building must account for the possibilities of sea level rise and flooding and the mitigation of those possibilities within their design for construction. The Kidcare bill passed; a subsidized child health insurance policy for families that are not qualified for Medicaid. Contingent of the Governor's approval, the Phase 1 South Miami septic to sewer conversion program for $1.8 million dollars were approved in appropriations. $350,000 was obtained for Disability Theater Enrichment Program. Also antiviolence initiative funding was received and $2.5 million dollars for the Underline Project.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: Captain Larry Corbin was awarded Officer of Month for his involvement in capturing two violent criminals. Three new officers that were recently sworn in have begun their field training as of Monday, May 15, 2023. The electronics recycling event will be held on Sunday, May 21st. The Town Center Advisory Board had their first meeting on May 11, 2023. The Town Hall Meeting will be held on May 18, 2023. The Budget & Finance Committee are actively meeting.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Regarding the parking garage, Mr. Recio reported that they have the survey and the amendment to the condominium declarations that need to be signed and recorded. An objection has been raised by the owner in the corner with regards to the ownership of the ramp. Mayor Fernández made a motion to authorize the city attorneys to file an action for declaratory judgement. The motion was seconded by Vice Mayor Bonich and Commissioner Liebman. The motion passed unanimously.

body: Mr. Recio read the quasi-judicial procedures and swore in the individuals that will speak on this item. All members of the Commission acknowledge their ex-parte communications with Dorolyn Dean. Vice Mayor Bonich and Commissioner Liebman also had ex-parte communications with Horace Feliu. Hank Flores, Planning Director, gave the staff report on this item and recommend approval with the conditions stated in the report. Yajaira Fuentes, applicant for this item, addressed the Commission and asked for approval. The following individuals spoke during the public hearing on this item: Dorolyn Dean, Gabe Edmond, Jeanette Benjamin, Leigh Emerson Smith, Antoinette Fischer, Reynolds Martin and Levy Kelly. After the public hearing, Ms. Fuentes and her attorney David Miller addressed the Commission for rebuttal of the speakers. title: City Manager's Report
body: Deputy City Manager Samantha Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: Regarding the monthly police recruitment update, all Communications positions are filled, one police officer applicant background is being done and should be completed in two weeks and four applicants are currently processing and they are due to graduate from the academy on July 21, 2023. On June 19, 2023, city hall will be closed in observance of Juneteenth Holiday.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio reported that the Stunna's Fit agreement will be on the June 20, 2023 agenda for the Commission's approval. The Special Meeting for June 20, 2023 was scheduled for 12:00 Noon. Regarding the parking garage, they are working on the declaration documents. This item was also added to the June 20, 2023 Commission meeting. Regarding the four Miami-Dade County legislation notifications received in May, two don't have anything to do with the City. The other two involves the City. One is a municipal campaign report law that requires campaign reports are to be place on the City's website. The last one involves a technical amendment to the Florida Building Code that requires buildings that have more than one unit and one water meter, they would have to also have two submeters.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Calle mentioned that he is going to sponsor the city clerk's contract at the next meeting; and stated that he met with Miami-Dade College Idea Center about establishing an entrepreneur network in the City. Commissioner Corey said the Homeless Trust is likely to fund tri-city effort for case management along US 1 corridor. Vice Mayor Bonich recognized Carlo Tassi, the owner of European Corner who recently passed away; and congratulated Janel Rodriguez of South Miami High School on her acceptance to the United States Airforce Academy. Mayor Fernández mentioned that he had a meeting with Miami-Dade County Mayor regarding city hall RFP and a possible collaboration through an Interlocal Agreement, annexation, Manor Land culvert financing, South Miami Plaza food quality and septic to sewer financing.

body: Mr. Recio explained the terms of the agreement. He stated that a conditional Business Tax Receipt (BTR) will be issued, subject to very strict conditions that are mandatory that must comply with the Code, comply with the noise ordinance, as well as the no outdoor commercial activities and the operating hours. The BTR will last until December 31, 2023 and then Stunna's would relocate. If Stunna's violate the agreement, the BTR can be revoked. There is also a letter of credit that they would need to file with the City for $35,000.00 to aid in enforcement cost, in the event they do not cease operations. Kyle Teal, attorney for Stunna's, thanked the Commission for their assistance with the agreement. Moved by Commissioner Corey, seconded by Commissioner Liebman, the motion to approve as amended with the addendum, RESOLUTION NO. 072-23-16005 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, APPROVING A SETTLEMENT AND COMPLIANCE AGREEMENT WITH STUNNAS FIT, LLC AND GABRIEL VARONA RELATING TO THE PROPERTY LOCATED AT 6600 SW 62ND AVENUE AND PENDING COURT ACTIONS AND CIVIL INFRACTIONS REGARDING OPERATIONS ON THE PROPERTY; AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE SETTLEMENT AND COMPLIANCE AGREEMENT; PROVIDING FOR AUTHORIZATION AND IMPLEMENTATION AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:            Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:            None

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: The City's request for additional funding for septic to sewer made it into the House budget for $1,750,000.00, but still must go to the Senate for approval. The Back-to-School Splash Bash is scheduled for Saturday, July 29, 2023 from 11:00 am to 1:00 pm at the Murray Park Aquatic Center. Miami-Dade County is ready to install the Low- Pressure Force Main (LPFM) at South Miami Park, it will be a 4-week project. At Dante Fascell Park, the Tennis Court Rebuild and Resurface Project is about 54% completed. Fuchs Park improvements are 89% completed. Vice Mayor Robert C. Welsh, Jr. Park improvements are 83% completed and there was an item added for safe access to the school. The Miami-Dade TREO Project has begun again at the South Miami Metrorail Station. Regarding the Avalon Bay project, the demolition is in process. South Miami Plaza Job Fair is scheduled for Wednesday, July 26, 2023 at 6:00 pm.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio updated the Commission on the following: South Miami Parking Garage deeds were finalized and recorded. The Planning Study workshop needs to be scheduled. The Planning Study Workshop was scheduled for Monday, July 31, 2023 at 9:30 a.m. Commissioner Calle would like to have a Sunshine Meeting regarding city hall procurement options. It was suggested to add it to the meeting of July 31st. As a response to Mayor Fernández regarding the settlement with Stunna's Fit, Mr. Recio stated that Stunna's Fit is waiting for the final letter of credit from their bank.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks. Commissioner Corey reported that there was a successful Sensory Lab event held on Saturday, July 15, 2023. Commissioner Calle mentioned that construction of the piping for the bathrooms at South Miami Park has started. Commissioner Liebman thanked the Commission for working together and thanked the staff for the budget process. He also thanked the Budget & Finance Committee and the Town Advisory Board for their input with the budget. He spoke about the importance of the Placemakings for Sunset Drive. Mayor Fernández thanked staff all the work during the budget process.

title: CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
body: I)      CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: He acknowledge the Parks & Recreation staff as July was Parks & Recreation Month. Relating to the enhancement of the parking garage, the installations of electric vehicle charges have been completed and the installation of the security cameras have been completed. The After-School Program registration has begun. The Football and Cheer Program kicks off August 11th. The tennis courts at Dante Fascell are 90% completed. There are four mini libraries throughout the parks system, with the newest installation at Van Smith Park. The Low Pressure Force Main (LPFM) at South Miami Park has been completed and restoration efforts are currently in progress. Fuchs Park improvements are 93% completed with full completion by August 16th. Vice Mayor Robert C. Welsh, Jr. Park is 90% completed and the ribbon-cutting ceremony is scheduled for Tuesday, August 8th at 4:00 pm. The Police Department has five vacancies and are actively recruiting through the academy. Sidewalk replacements and roadway resurfacing throughout the City are ongoing. Additional work at US1 and Sunset, is being done with the SOMI TREO building through the end of August. The demolition at the Avalon Project is almost complete.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias reported on the following: Two retirements and one hire in the Police Department for the reporting period, recruiting is ongoing. The unveiling of the Marshall Williamson Monument is scheduled for Friday, September 8th at 4:00 pm at Marshall Williamson Park. 9/11 National Day of Service and Remembrance Clean-up at All America Park will be held on Monday, September 11th. The Aquatic Center closes for the season on Saturday, September 30th. The City received renewal of funds for the senior weekend meals program. The City launched SoMi Connect a mobile app for residents to report incidents. A video was shown to show how the app works.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Calle mentioned the kids marketplace event at Sunset Place that will be held November 4th. Commissioner Corey mentioned the groundbreaking at Avalon Bay and the unveiling of the Marshall Williamson monument. With the City changing, he would like to recognize other historical people of the City. Commissioner Liebman recognized Captain Larry Corbin as Acting Police Chief; thanked and recognized Guirla Dodard for her service on the Planning Board; and mentioned the Avalon Bay groundbreaking event. Vice Mayor Bonich also mentioned the Avalon Bay event. Mayor Fernández apologized for missing the Avalon Bay event; thanked Capt. Corbin for his services as Acting Chief and congratulated the city manager on the process and the hiring of a new police chief; and mentioned the Phase II of the Underline groundbreaking event. He also presented an updated proposal from Freebee and a proposal from Uber.

title: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, ADOPTING A PROPOSED MILLAGE RATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR COMMENCING OCTOBER 1, 2023 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 (“FISCAL YEAR 2023/2024”), WHICH AMOUNT MAY BE AMENDED AT THE FIRST OR SECOND READING; AND ADOPTING THE FINAL MILLAGE RATE ON SECOND READING; PROVIDING FOR CORRECTIONS; SEVERABILITY; CONFLICTS; AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE. 3/5 (CITY MANAGER)

votes.motion: approve ORDINANCE NO. 14-23-2465 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, ADOPTING A PROPOSED MILLAGE RATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR COMMENCING OCTOBER 1, 2023 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 (“FISCAL YEAR 2023/2024”), WHICH AMOUNT MAY BE AMENDED AT THE FIRST OR SECOND READING; AND ADOPTING THE FINAL MILLAGE RATE ON SECOND READING; PROVIDING FOR CORRECTIONS; SEVERABILITY; CONFLICTS; AND AN

body: Alfredo Riverol stated that the millage rate is 3.95 which rate is an 9.62% increase over the rolled back rate of 3.6034 mills. The changes that occurred since the first reading are as follows, reduced the contingency, by adding one police officer at $90,440, reduced the ad valorem by $124,025 which was the effect reducing from 3.99 to 3.95. Also the insurance premium was overbudgeted so that amount was reduced by $32,551. The public hearing on items #1 and #2 was opened and closed with no speakers. Attorney Arango read the following statement: the proposed millage rate of 3.9500 which exceeds the rollback rate of 3.6034 by 9.62% which is statutorily the property tax increase. The Commission asked that the city manager bring back the state and federal lobbyist contracts for discussion/approval at the October 3, 2023 City Commission meeting. Moved by Commissioner Liebman, seconded by Commissioner Corey, the motion to approve ORDINANCE NO. 14-23-2465 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, ADOPTING A PROPOSED MILLAGE RATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR COMMENCING OCTOBER 1, 2023 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 (“FISCAL YEAR 2023/2024”), WHICH AMOUNT MAY BE AMENDED AT THE FIRST OR SECOND READING; AND ADOPTING THE FINAL MILLAGE RATE ON SECOND READING; PROVIDING FOR CORRECTIONS; SEVERABILITY; CONFLICTS; AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:            Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:            None

Mayor Fernández, Vice Mayor Bonich, Commissioner Calle and Commissioner Corey all had ex-parte communications with the applicant. title: City Manager's Report
body: Mr. Iglesias welcomed Development Services Director Suramy Cabrera to her first meeting and mentioned that Chief Reo Hatfield starts on November 8, 2023. Deputy Manager Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: The City will join the American Legion for a Veteran's Day event. The Mayor's State of the City and the Chief's Swearing-In ceremony will be held on Monday, November 13, 2023 at Area Stage in the Shops at Sunset Place. The Thanksgiving Give-a-way is scheduled for Friday, November 17, 2023 for residents from 6:00 pm - 8:00 pm at the community center. She also gave an update on the hiring of the following positions: Communications and Marketing Manager position, Community Affairs Manager, Public Works Director and Human Resources and Risk Manager. Mayor Fernandez mentioned that Dante Fascell parking lot is being used for bus pickup for kids in area schools and wanted to know if there is a process in place because of liability issues. Also wanted to know if there are procedures for parking cars in the right-of-way around construction areas.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio reported on the following: Regarding the Mandelstam litigation, this is being handled by insurance counsel. A motion to dismiss on behalf of the City was filed in October 2022, and it was granted today. However, the judge gave the plaintiff 20 days to file a third amended complaint and made it clear that this will be the last complaint filed on this case. Mayor Fernandez asked when the right-of-way improvements agreement for the Avalon Bay project will come back for Commission approval. Mr. Recio answered that it should be on the first meeting in December.

body: Attorney Recio swore in speakers for items# 8-11. Mayor Fernández, Vice Mayor Bonich, Commissioner Calle, and Commissioner Liebman disclosed that they had contact with Mr. Perez and Mr. Vadia regarding the project. Mark Alvarez, of the Corradino Group presented the items. He mentioned that there was a small change since first reading, for further protection for the Live Local Act. There are four bonuses for the gateway zone, the one closest to US1. It has been reduced to 12 floors from 17. Mr. Recio stated another change was the penalty amount. title: December 2023 & January 2024 City Commission meetings
body: The Commission decided to cancel the January 2, 2024 City Commission Meeting. L)      COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS Vice Mayor Bonich asked that the Commission agenda is received earlier so that they have time to review items. Mayor Fernández suggested staff propose a schedule for 2024 for submittal deadlines for agenda items. Commissioner Calle asked for a follow-up on the marketing plan. He also asked that the Commission explore having an assistant that works for the Commission. Commissioner Corey spoke about creating a longtime strategy plan for the Hometown District. Mayor Fernández thanked Interval International for their 27-year commitment for the Thanksgiving give away, as well as Baptist Hospital. He also thanked the staff for the successful State of the City event. Commissioner Liebman stated that he is appreciative of the Mayor for flying back intown to attend the Commission meeting and thanked all City staff for everything. title: City Manager's Report
body: Deputy City Manger Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: Registration is open for winter break camp for December 26 - 29, 2023 and January 2 -5, 2024. The following are upcoming events: Christmas Tree decorating party at the Senior Center on Wednesday, December 6, 2023, Friday, December 15, 2023, Movie Night at South Miami Park, and Saturday, December 16, 2023 is the toy drive. Job offers have been extended to three candidates for HR Risk Manager, Communications and Marketing Manager, and Community Affairs Manager, and all have been accepted. Also, a video was shown of the progress of the Avalon Bay project.

title: Discussion on enforcement action for the property located at 5660 SW 58 Place
body: Mr. Recio reported on the code enforcement issues with the property at 5660 SW 58 Place. Ms. Arango stated that the City has three options, 1) go back to the Special Magistrate to secure a more enforceable order; 2) protentional litigation to seek an injunction, and 3) a code amendment to create a process to allow the city manager to make a determination if there is an emanate danger for public health and safety welfare to order an abatement. After the discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Calle and seconded by Mayor Fernandez to have the attorney move to do injunctive relief and a code modification. The motion passed unanimously.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: Mayor Fernandez thanked staff for an excellent Elves Parade. He also mentioned a great meetings in Tallahassee with Senator President-Elect Ben Albritton, Representative Demi Busatta Cabrera, Representative Sam Garrison and Representative Daniel Perez. Commissioner Calle stated that he had a productive meeting with Senator Alexis Calatayud. Commissioner Liebman spoke about an undesirable type of crowd leaving an establishment in the City; Freebee’s wait time; the successful Elves Parade; and spoke of the passing of Thomas Talby. Vice Mayor Bonich sent her condolences to Alex Vadia on the loss of his father.

body: Deputy City Manager Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: The Finance Department was awarded the GFOA Certificate of Achievement for excellence in financial reporting for fiscal year 2022. The City is hosting the MLK Freedom Breakfast on Monday, January 15, 2024 at Jean Willis Park. There will be no garbage collections on Monday, December 25th or Monday, January 1st, it will be collected on Tuesday, December 26th and January 2nd and Tuesday's route will be collected on Wednesday. body: Mr. Recio stated regarding South Miami Park, a deed search was done, and no deed restrictions were found. Also, a title search was completed, and no restrictions were found. Ms. Arango noted that in 2005 when the City acquired the property from the YMCA, the City paid $2.75 million and typically there are no deed restrictions for fair market value. Mayor Fernández suggested that the attorneys research the complete land development records on the property, so everything is clear. Mr. Recio stated that he will provide the Commission with a proposed ERPB flow chart and if can get some feedback at the February 6th sunshine meeting.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission reports: Commissioner Calle spoke about the Porche Event. Commissioner Corey spoke about the cost of burying the power lines in the Hometown District. Commissioner Liebman spoke about panhandling and the rights of the business owners when it comes to this. Vice Mayor Bonich also spoke about the panhandling and what can be done better to deal with this issue. She also mentioned the successful MLK breakfast event. Mayor Fernández asked for an update on the following: Bird scooter program, FREEBEE now that they are operating with Tesla's, and RFP for transportation services. He mentioned that a Metro Connect presentation was done at the Metro South Center and requested that information regarding Metro Connect is added to our website and that a presentation is done at the South Miami Plaza. He also stated that he wants to work with the city attorney regarding an interlocal on traffic mitigation measures. Also requested an ordinance regarding eliminating construction hours on holidays and addressing staging areas doing construction.

votes.motion: approve as amended RESOLUTION NO. 022-24-16127 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA [GRANTING APPROVAL OF/DENYING] AN APPLICATION FOR FINAL PLAT APPROVAL PURSUANT TO SECTION 20-4.2 OF THE LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE SEEKING TO SUBDIVIDE A PROPERTY WITHIN THE LOW DENSITY SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL (RS-3) ZONING DISTRICT LOCATED AT 7709 SW 67 AVENUE; PROVIDING FOR CONDITIONS; CORRECTI

body: Mr. Recio read the procedures for this quasi-judicial item and swore in the speakers for this item. Regarding ex-parte communications, Mayor Fernández stated he received a text from Tomas Cabrezio asking for favorable consideration for this item. Commissioner Calle mentioned that he spoke with a constituent about options about this property. Mr. Recio mentioned that in Section 3, it should be amended to state before the conditions starts except to the extent modified below and four (4) conditions are added: d) Prior to building permit, the applicant shall execute and record in public records in Miami-Dade County a restrictive covenant in a form approved by and subject to review and approval of the city manager and city attorney which contains all commitments made in conditions imposed as part of the approval of the final plat. e) The applicant shall submit a grading plan, landscaping plan, and tree disposition plan in addition to all other required plans to the Environmental Review & Preservation Board for review of each of the three homes. f) The eastern most lot shall be limited to one story which shall be permitted as per code, a building coverage of 35% of the lot area and impervious coverage of 50% of the lot area. g) The applicant may alter the conceptual plan that has been submitted in any manner that meets code requirements. Marcus Lightfoot, Senior Planner/Zoning Administrator, presented the item to the Commission. Eddy Baker, representative for the applicant, addressed the Commission regarding this item. The public hearing on this item was opened and closed with no speakers. Moved by Commissioner Liebman, seconded by Commissioner Corey, the motion to approve as amended RESOLUTION NO. 022-24-16127 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA [GRANTING APPROVAL OF/DENYING] AN APPLICATION FOR FINAL PLAT APPROVAL PURSUANT TO SECTION 20-4.2 OF THE LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE SEEKING TO SUBDIVIDE A PROPERTY WITHIN THE LOW DENSITY SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL (RS-3) ZONING DISTRICT LOCATED AT 7709 SW 67 AVENUE; PROVIDING FOR CONDITIONS; CORRECTIONS; SEVERABILITY; AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:             Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:             None

title: City Manager's Report
body: Deputy City Manager Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: She gave an update on the Avalon Bay Project. Registration for summer camp and Grey Ghost Football and Cheerleading has opened. Upcoming activities: Senior's St. Patrick Day party is scheduled for Friday, March 15, 2024; the Easter Egg Hunt at Murry Park is Saturday, March 16, 2024. Regarding appropriations, on the federal level, the sanitary and sewer extension project submitted by Rep. Salazar for $1.75 million was included in the bill and will be voted on Friday, March 8, 2024. At the State level, request for funding for the police radios $500,000, bike lanes $800,000, septic to sewer $1.5 million, Manner Lane culvert replacement $235,000 were all included in the State's budget. Mr. Iglesias thanked staff for successfully handling two big events in the City, the Arts Festival and the Unity Festival at the same time. Commissioner Calle asked for an annexation update at the next meeting.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of Commission remarks: Commissioner Corey mentioned that after contacting residents regarding the ballot question, they seem to be happy with the City Commission. Commissioner Calle commented on the successful Arts and Unity Festivals. He met with Miami-Dade County Commissioner Kevin Cabrera and updated him on what's happening in the City. Mayor Fernández asked for an update on the status of the septic to sewer procurement report for the next agenda. Thanked everyone for working on the budget items for the State's budget. He mentioned that he has spoken to Meg Daly of the Underline and would like to meet about jointly designing or modify the plans to take advantage of possibly relocating Jean Willis Park. He shared that he is meeting with Miami-Dade Commissioner Raquel Regalado to discuss the City's priorities.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Deputy City Manager Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: Starting July 1st the Senior Center are extending their hours to 3:00 pm to allow for some afternoon activities. The annual 4th of July event will be held at Palmer Park from 5:00 pm - 9:00 pm. July 13th is Reo's Bike Rodeo hosted by the Police Department from 10:00 am - 1:00 pm. Following that, SOMI Second Saturdays will be held with a country western theme.

title: CITY ATTORNEY’S REPORT
body: Mr. Recio asked for a conflict of interest to be waived regarding Baptist Hospital's urgent care facility. One of their partners represents them but Ms. Arango and him do not work with them. It was moved by Vice Mayor Bonich and seconded by Commissioner Calle to waive the conflict of interest. The motion passed unanimously.

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: Commissioner Corey spoke about the monthly unhoused meetings, that are held once a month at the library. Commissioner Calle spoke about the Father's Day event. He also spoke about the Underline Project, working on getting people employed for the different construction projects. Also mentioned working together with the different boards and committees. Mayor Fernández shared condolences of long-time employee George Green, retiree who recently passed away.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Ms. Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: Construction has been completed on the South Miami Park new field light improvement project. On July 24th there will be a Round Robin Pickle Ball Tournament at Marshall Williamson Park. Saturday, July 27th is the Back to School Splash Bash Event at Murray Park. A workshop that was coordinated by Mayor Fernández in collaboration with Transit Alliance will be held at South Miami Senior Plaza on July 30th at 10:00 am and at Metro South at 1:00 pm. This workshop is to give information about the upcoming changes related to the Better Bus Project and Metro Connect. Bank of America will host a Literacy Challenge at the Mobley Building on July 23, 2023 for 7th through 12th graders, an initiative championed by Commissioner Calle and Miami-Dade County Commissioner Raquel Regalado.

title: Dr. Tina Scott, Medical Director of South Miami Children's Clinic - Miami Foundation Saltwater Fellowship Award Recipient
body: Dr. Scott was recognized with a Certificate of Recognition as a Miami Foundation Saltwater Fellowship Award Recipient. The Saltwater Fellowship, named after South Florida’s historic underground railroad, is a 12-month program offering community-based skills training, access to equity labs, coaching, wellness retreats, and $100,000 in unrestricted grant dollars over two years to an inaugural cohort of 10 advocacy organization founders and CEOs.

title: Police to Citizen Portal (P2C) - Chief Hatfield
body: Chief Hatfield presented a PowerPoint presentation on Police to Citizen Portal (P2C). The P2C site allows the public to report certain types of offenses online without the need or assistance from a sworn or civilian member.

title: Park Month Proclamation
body: The Commission presented the Parks, Recreation and Culture Department a proclamation in observance of July being Park Month. The years theme "Where you belong". At this time, it was moved by Commissioner Called and seconded by Commissioner Liebman to add the add-on item to the agenda. The motion passed unanimously.

Moved by Commissioner Calle, seconded by Commissioner Corey, the motion to approve RESOLUTION NO. 097-24-16202 OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, CALLING FOR A SPECIAL ELECTION FOR THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 5, 2024, CONCURRENT WITH THE GENERAL ELECTION, FOR THE PURPOSE OF SUBMITTING TO THE ELECTORATE A BOND REFERENDUM REGARDING THE ISSUANCE OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS BY THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED SIXTY-FIVE MILLION ($65,000,000.00) DOLLARS FOR THE PURPOSE OF ACQUIRING, CONSTRUCTING, RECONSTRUCTING, IMPROVING AND EQUIPPING VARIOUS CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS, REAL PROPERTY, AND INFRASTRUCTURE FOR PARKS AND RECREATION, PUBLIC WORKS, AND PUBLIC SAFETY; PROVIDING FOR PUBLICATION OF NOTICE OF SUCH REFERENDUM; PROVIDING REQUISITE BALLOT LANGUAGE FOR SUBMISSION TO THE ELECTORATE; PROVIDING FOR THE CITY CLERK TO UTILIZE THE SERVICES OF MIAMI-DADE COUNTY SUPERVISOR OF ELECTIONS FOR THE SPECIAL ELECTION; PROVIDING FOR CORRECTIONS; PROVIDING FOR IMPLEMENTATION AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 4 - 1 vote: Yea:           Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:           Commissioner Liebman

body: The Commission paused the item, while researching the language of last ballot question. During this time the Commission directed the city manager to accept the cash bond waiver from the Related Group for the Art in Public Places and bring back at the next meeting a resolution ratifying the waiver. Also, it was moved by Vice Mayor Bonich and seconded by Commissioner Calle to cancel the August 6, 2024 City Commission meeting. The motion passed unanimously. The Commission also discussed the RFP process for the City Hall Redevelopment Project once the proposals are received. After the discussion, the Commission decided on the following language: Four-year term of office for City Mayor Shall the Charter be amended to set the Mayor’s term consistent with the City Commissioners’ term of four years, beginning with the 2026 South Miami General Election? Moved by Commissioner Liebman, seconded by Vice Mayor Bonich, the motion to approve as amended RESOLUTION NO. 098-24-16203 OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, CALLING FOR A CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI SPECIAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 5, 2024 FOR THE PURPOSE OF SUBMITTING TO THE ELECTORATE A PROPOSED AMENDMENT TO SECTION 2(A) OF ARTICLE V, “ELECTIONS,” OF THE CITY CHARTER TO INCREASE THE TERM OF OFFICE FOR THE OFFICE OF CITY MAYOR TO FOUR (4) YEARS BEGINNING WITH THE 2026 SOUTH MIAMI GENERAL ELECTION; PROVIDING FOR NOTICE OF ELECTION; PROVIDING REQUISITE BALLOT LANGUAGE AND CHARTER AMENDMENT TEXT FOR SUBMISSION TO THE ELECTORATE; PROVIDING FOR THE CITY CLERK TO UTILIZE THE SERVICES OF MIAMI-DADE COUNTY SUPERVISOR OF ELECTIONS FOR THE SPECIAL ELECTION; AND PROVIDING FOR INCLUSION IN THE CHARTER; PROVIDING FOR SEVERABILITY; CORRECTIONS; AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:          Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:          None

title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: The following is a summary of the Commission discussion: Vice Mayor Bonich spoke about the school zone cameras and asked if the Commission can revisit the hours of enforcing the speed limit. She also mentioned having the Commission discuss the various speed limit rates on Sunset Drive at a future meeting. She clarified for the record that she is not in support of raising anyone's taxes regarding her support of the $65,000,000 bond question on the ballot. Chief Reo Hatfield gave the times of the speed enforcement of the different school zones. He mentioned that it is not enforced on non-school days, it is enforced 30 minutes before school starts and 30 minutes after school ends. Commissioner Calle spoke about the greet meeting/discussion that he and Mayor Fernández had with the Wirtz family in Chicago as it relates to their property development in South Miami. Mayor Fernández thanked the public for the approval of the charter modification that was passed August 20, 2024, and for his reelection without opposition.

body: City Attorney Recio read the following statement: This item seeks approval of a development agreement under Section 163 Florida Local Government Development Agreement Act and section 20-12.13 of the City's Land Development Code, this is the first of two readings. If approved tonight the second reading is intended to take place on October 15, 2024. The resolution for the development agreement is a quasi legislative item, never the less a public hearing under the statute. In an abundance of caution in order to afford the most do process possible for all parties, without waiving the Commission's position of the resolution the development agreement is in fact legislative in nature. The City will frame the discussion in the following parameters: the city attorney will give a brief overview of the development agreement and context, the developer may make a presentation, the public should be given an opportunity to comment, the developer can address the comments and at that point the public hearing should be closed and the Commission can deliberate on the discussion. Anyone that would speak on this item, the city attorney swore them in. Richard Perez, representing the developer, addressed the Commission as it relates to the development agreement. The following spoke during the public hearing on this item: Susana Mendive, Gary Simon, Lee Jacobs and Ken Hensel. Moved by Commissioner Liebman, seconded by Vice Mayor Bonich, the motion to approve A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH MIAMI, FLORIDA, APPROVING A DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT WITH SUNSET OPPORTUNITIES B1, LLC, AND SUNSET C1, LLC, FOR THE 10.09-ACRE PROPERTY KNOWN AS “SUNSET PLACE” LOCATED AT 5701-5795 SW 72 STREET (SUNSET DRIVE) IN THE DOWNTOWN SOMI (DS) DISTRICT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 163.3220 THROUGH 163.3243, FLORIDA STATUTES, AND SECTION 20-12.13 OF THE LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE; AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT AND ALL OTHER SUPPORTING INSTRUMENTS REQUIRED BY THE LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE FOR DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPERTY; PROVIDING FOR CORRECTIONS; IMPLEMENTATION; SEVERABILITY; AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE passed by a 5 - 0 vote: Yea:             Mayor Fernández Vice Mayor Bonich Commissioner Liebman Commissioner Corey Commissioner Calle Nay:             None

body: City Attorney Recio read the quasi-judicial procedures and swore in speakers for this item. Commissioner Calle disclosed ex-parte communication with the attorney for the applicant regarding tree mitigation. City Attorney Recio mentioned that he made the following amendments to the item: Condition 2 should start with, If required by the City; and Condition 6 replace with the following wording: Applicant to provide a Surveyor’s Affidavit, in form and substance acceptable to the City Attorney, prior to recording of the final plat, to confirm legal description shown on the final plat describes the same properties as the legal descriptions on the deeds of the subject parcels; and James Williams, attorney for the applicant to address the Commission with regards to the tree mitigation. title: RESOLUTION(S) PUBLIC HEARING(S)
body: Attorney Recio explained and stated the quasi procedures for items #15 and #16 and swore in speakers. Both items were taken together. Commissioner Liebman, Vice Mayor Bonich, Mayor Fernández, Commissioner Corey and Commissioner Calle all had ex-parte communications with the Principles of the project. Mark Alvarez, The Corradino Group, gave the staff report for the items and recommending approval with the following six conditions as outlined in the memo, except for the Impervious area is to be compliant the requirements of Section 12.9. Attorney Recio gave a history of the process of approvals for this project. Attorney Recio also mentioned that a supplement memo for the Development Agreement revisions was presented with changes from the first public hearing. Please note the memo will be attached to the resolution. Richard Perez, of Midtown Development, gave a presentation of the proposed Sunset Place Project. Thomas Heatherwick, Designer of the Sunset Place Project, presented the design concepts of the Project. The following individuals spoke during the public hearings on items #15 and #16: Pierre Assaf, Alvaro Rodriguez, Maurice Habif, EJ Martinez, Sultan Albarq, Ed Boas, Ramon Fernández, John Edward Smith, Jorge Ramos, Matt Childers, Andreina Cecilia Lara, Helen Feelins, Jesus Saul, Ken Hensel, Andrew Kerney, Manny Alonso, Michael Bond, Andres Cela, Maria Tors, and Laura Bonich. After the public hearing on this item, the Commission discussed the item.

Also, in attendance were Chip Iglesia, City Manager, Samantha Fraga-Lopez, Deputy City Manager, Tony Recio, City Attorney, Lillian Arango, City Attorney, and Nkenga A. Payne, City Clerk.

title: PRESENTATIONS
body: Commissioner Liebman A farewell video presentation for Commissioner Liebman for his twelve plus years of service on the City Commission was shown. The following individuals spoke kind words to Commissioner Liebman: Shari Kamali, Mike Vonderherf, Jeff Bass, Andy Korge, James McCants, Steven Alexander, and Jose Fuentes. Commissioner Corey presented Commissioner Liebman with a replica of the plaque that will be placed in the Columbia Sculpture Garden in Dante Fascell Park.

title: City Manager's Report
body: Mrs. Fraga-Lopez reported on the following: South Miami Park updates - the picnic shelter project is scheduled to be completed in the upcoming week; the landscape improvements on the perimeter of the property are complete; the turf fields ribbon cutting will be scheduled in December. Upcoming events: SOMI Second Saturday, Battle of the Bands on November 9th and Monday, November 11th Veteran's Day celebration at Veterans Park. The Finance Department has again obtained Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) Certificate of Achievement of Excellence in finance reporting for fiscal year 2023.

body: Mark Alvarez, of The Corradino Group, presented the TSDD that incorporated everything from the first reading, Planning Board comments, as well as comments from the workshop. The following spoke during the public hearing on this item: Dr. Steve Hellegua, Marcos Puente, Adam Freeman, Javier Avino, Jeff Bass, and Alex Ferras. The meeting was extended to 11:30 pm, with a motion by Commissioner Liebman and seconded by Commissioner Corey. The motion passed unanimously. After the discussion on this item, the Commission decided to hear the final reading on this item on December 10, 2024. The map amendments will go to the Planning Board at a special meeting on December 3, 2024, with the first reading at the Commission meeting on December 10, 2024. The second reading of the map amendments will be heard at the February 18, 2025 City Commission meeting, provided that the State has reviewed and sent back comments. It was moved by Commissioner Calle and seconded by Commissioner Corey to remand this item back to the Planning Board, with all feedback that was heard tonight, at their special meeting on December 3, 2024. The motion passed unanimously. body: The following individuals spoke during the public hearing on this item: Nick Noto, Adam Freeman, Javier Avino, Jeff Bass, Alexander Cimo, Jerry Proctor, Don Vitek, Joey Weston, Hank Courtney, and Joe Huleaqua. After an extensive discussion, Mayor Fernández and seconded by Commissioner Calle to incorporate the following amendments to the ordinance: remove the 150 student cap, incorporate the TDR program with suggestions submitted by Commissioner Rodriguez, and Commissioner Calle's suggestions. Commissioner Bonich: nay; Commissioner Rodriguez: yea; Commissioner Calle: yea; Vice Mayor Corey: nay; Mayor Fernández: yea. The motion passed by a 3-2 vote. title: COMMISSION REPORTS, DISCUSSION & REMARKS
body: Commissioner Bonich spoke about pausing the banding for the City. After some discussion, Mayor Fernández asked to let the Town Advisory Board discuss it and bring this back at the end of January. Commissioner Rodriguez sent condolences to the family of Nolan King a teen who was tragically murdered in the City. Mayor Fernández thanked the manager for a recent act of kindness.
